I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the land, match the local weather, and keep the work manageable. I am 63, so I will not spread myself across too many crops or try risky changes. Winter wheat is already the backbone of my year, and after harvest I can plant summer maize right away, so the land does not sit idle. I will use improved seed because I want stable yield and better resistance, but I will still manage the field in the simple way I trust: base fertilizer before planting, one or two topdressings for nitrogen, irrigation at the key stages, and pesticide only when pressure is real. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my labor and machinery conditions. My aim is steady output, lower risk, and work I can finish on time.
